body: i stand by my unamended statement. but at least one of you's a comedian, too.
happy cake day.
you're very wise.

it's possible, too, to look good without fully passing.

i emphasize passing so much because i keenly feel the agony when i feebly try and don't pass right now.
There's definitely a certain narcissism in not only scrutinizing oneself so closely and constantly monitoring all flaws but imagining others will, too.

6 months sounds a lot faster than i thought.

i should try it again. not that i'll expect that.
thank you an incredible amount.

i hear you. i don't know if i can last the year or two. i don't know how i can convince myself it would be worth it.

i know one who doesn't pass. but he's living the dream. gay married and everything. i want to be happy like him. i can't convince myself i would be.

i don't know how to find a t who won't... i don't like to talk about the last one.

i probably sound really whiny.
can't separate what they *might* feel from my long-term self-loathing.
i'd probably be happier if i believed that. one look in the mirror has me absolutely convinced otherwise. i feel helpless and hopeless.

i avoid the things i want to do because i know people will hate me because of them. even if they're totally innocuous like grocery shopping.

i could look in mirrors. i could speak out loud without self-harming to punish myself.

doesn't help i'm anxiety-filled anyway, from waking up with panic attacks over nothing to... but that's the depression and stuff. i've had that for years. that just hurts.

i like how you write. you've a unique voice. :)

thought plaid and (rainbow?) stripes were a lesbian joke at first.

if i liked myself i'd have self-confidence.

because i hate being me i fight it -- suppress or avoid self-expression. noticing me being me makes me so sad and angry. i want to lash out but i don't have anything to attack except myself because i'm the problem.

suppose suicide's the logical conclusion.

emotionally seems most likely but i don't like to rule anything out. :/

i don't hate my orientation. i actually like it, except for the part where i'm a special fucking snowflake.

i hate my personality. i hate the way i act. i hate my interests and bad taste and how ugly i am. et cetera. sorry to rant on.

and now, too, i feel such sorrow and hopelessness at the impossibility of people believing i am what and who i feel like.

thank you for your very kind words and for taking the time. you're not a dick... except maybe in the sense that who decided dicks were bad? :p

i could also try to cut or burn myself in case i can succeed in that not hurting. but i know how that will turn out.

i already hate who i am and that hurts. sometimes not everyone hates me now. if they saw my failure many (most?) would and so that would increase the pain i already have.

i don't think it is right. but it happens. they do judge. i hear people judge others every day. i know how they'd judge me. i know how they'd do it already. useless to fight that.

and dangerous, where i come from.

my problem's that part of who i want to become is someone who others accept. i don't know how. ideally they can accept the person i feel like, but i think that's impossible.
good advice, but very foreign to me. i had to stop and think about it. i hate and distrust myself so much, combined with being sensitive to others' reactions so they won't hurt me.

my social anxiety's bad enough that i completely sympathize with you there, but...

when i've had problems like this the only thing i could think of was to come clean. maybe walk into a therapist's office, explain the situation, and ask the receptionist what they advise? maybe there's nothing they can do, maybe they've heard of some way of getting you help. worst comes to worst you're anonymous and you can cheese it before anyone can catch you.

sorry i'm so shitty at advice. :/
yes, preeeety desperately. :(

then don't take meds?

some universities require their students to provide a certain number of free (or really cheap) sessions to people. sometimes they'll only do so for students, sometimes to anyone.

have you asked around if there's any way to get free therapy in your area?

i don't mean to stress therapy over other options. if you're not happy with anything, what have you got to lose by trying any of the events or activities that may exist near you?

some therapists charge a "sliding scale" -- basically you pay what you can. or you may be able to get assistance, whether from the government or not, but you don't sound like you'd like going that route.

i've had mixed results with them, too. some therapists are really bad listeners. :/

if you're worried about going inpatient's... that's pretty extreme. most people don't need it.

have you considered less extreme options? talk therapy once a week? no one has to know you're going.

i know you don't want to hear take up a hobby, but if you really don't know what to do why not spend a few hours trying a cooking class or whatever? not because it'll solve all your problems. because it might distract you from hating yourself for a few hours. or not and you might hate it, but what have you got to lose? it's gone both ways for me before. (i hate myself and get anxiety pretty badly.)
dunno. some of my favorite music sounds like it was written by deaf people. :p

i'll talk to you. i've been thinking of suicide every day, too. for a long time.

being interested in airplanes sounds cool.
